categories_checked.note: su.dk: SU grant, SU loan, equal-status routes for foreign citizens (EU worker, 5 years residence, Danish-rule routes), 2026 rates, SU reform from 1 Jan 2027.
Boligstøtte (Udbetaling Danmark) via borger.dk student page and lifeindenmark housing-benefit page.
Free public healthcare after CPR registration (Study in Denmark). No separate student health subsidy found.
Ungdomskort (ungdomskort.dk) eligibility and 2026 price. Rejsekort has no student discount on its homepage.
Personal allowance (personfradrag) on skat.dk tax-card page. Student-specific tax relief not found.
No subsidy tied to student work found; the related rules (SU earnings limit, EU-worker route to SU) are in bureaucracy.json and state_grant_loan.

su.dk 'SU i udlandet': SU can be taken abroad for part of a Danish degree (outgoing). No Danish top-up for INCOMING Erasmus students found on the pages opened (KU, DTU, AU scholarship pages); host-country search was limited.
The main student measures found (SU, boligstøtte, Ungdomskort) are national. A dedicated search for regional/municipal student grants was not done: the shared web-search budget ran out.
University of Copenhagen, DTU and Aarhus University scholarship/tuition-waiver pages (all for non-EU/EEA fee-paying master's students).

items.name_local: SU (Statens Uddannelsesstøtte) – ligestilling som arbejdstager efter EU-retten
items.name_it: SU (borsa statale danese) per cittadini UE con status di lavoratore
items.description: EU/EEA and Swiss students can get the Danish state grant on equal terms with Danes if they have worker status under EU law: generally about 10-12 hours of paid work per week, for at least 10 consecutive weeks after approval and throughout the SU period (hours cannot be averaged across months). Assessed case by case; the approval letter states the hours required.

eligibility.min_work_hours: about 10-12 hours/week of paid work (40 h/month is generally not enough), 10 consecutive weeks to obtain the status, then continuously
eligibility.income_test: gross pay must reach a certain level; approved examples: DKK 125/hour + 12.5% holiday allowance, or DKK 120/hour + 12.5% with 11 h/week
other: enrolled in an SU-approved programme in Denmark
also subject to the SU earnings limit (fribeløb)

items.amount: DKK 7,426/month before tax if living away from parents (udeboende), higher education (2026); living with parents: base DKK 1,154/month + possible parent-income supplement (2026)
items.how_to_apply: Apply for SU and equal status in minSU (self-service); attach all employment contracts. Decision via Digital Post.
items.stackable: Can be combined with SU loan (SU-lån) and boligstøtte; income counts toward the SU earnings limit and the housing-benefit income test.
items.notes: su.dk does not explicitly address exchange students; 'degree' reflects that SU is for an SU-approved Danish programme. SU reform: for programmes started on or after 1 July 2025 the total SU frame drops from 70 to 58 monthly clips and support is tied to the programme's normed length, effective 1 January 2027.

interpretations.hypothesis: Reading A (encoded): SU requires enrolment in an SU-approved Danish programme, so it is for full-degree students; a one- or two-semester exchange student does not qualify.

Reading B: su.dk does not address exchange students explicitly; an EU exchange student who meets the worker condition is not expressly excluded, so eligibility must be confirmed with SU (Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen) before saying no.

items.name_local: SU – ligestilling efter ophold (EU-regler og danske regler)
items.name_it: SU per stranieri dopo anni di residenza o altri titoli
items.description: Without worker status, foreign citizens can still get SU on equal terms through other routes: under EU rules, 5 years of residence in Denmark or being the child/spouse/parent of an EU worker in Denmark; under Danish rules, e.g. 5 years of residence, 2 years of work in Denmark, having come to Denmark with your parents, or marriage to a Danish citizen.

eligibility.residence_requirement: e.g. at least 5 years of residence in Denmark (other routes listed on su.dk)
other: non-EU students on a study residence permit: check with the immigration authorities, receiving SU may affect the right to stay
equal status lapses after more than 2 years continuously abroad

items.amount: Same rates as Danish students: DKK 7,426/month before tax (udeboende, higher education, 2026)
items.how_to_apply: Apply for equal status and SU in minSU.
items.stackable: Combinable with SU loan and boligstøtte.

items.description: Students entitled to SU can additionally borrow a state study loan each month, choosing any amount up to the monthly maximum.

other: must be entitled to SU (Danish citizen or foreign citizen with equal status)

items.stackable: Taken together with the SU grant; repayable with interest (interest rate not stated on the page opened).
items.notes: SU reform (effective 1 Jan 2027, students starting on/after 1 July 2025): completion loans (slutlån) for up to 24 months in total.

items.description: Tax-free monthly housing benefit for tenants who live permanently in a rented home with its own kitchen. Amount depends on rent (excluding utilities), floor area, household size, and income and assets of the adults. A room in someone else's home without your own kitchen normally does not qualify; only one person per household can receive it.

eligibility.income_test: means-tested on household income and assets; recalculated monthly with Danish Tax Agency income data
eligibility.stay_duration: can apply even for a short stay, but must live in the home permanently
other: tenant named on the lease (not owner)
own kitchen or kitchenette
paid to a NemKonto, so a CPR number is in practice needed

items.amount: max DKK 1,194/month for non-pensioner renters without children (2026); DKK 4,201 with 1-3 children
items.how_to_apply: Apply digitally (lifeindenmark.dk / borger.dk); English guides exist for dorm rooms, rented rooms and rented homes. Letters from Udbetaling Danmark are in Danish.
items.stackable: Combinable with SU; SU and job income count in the income test. Can be kept during an exchange abroad if you do not sublet and return within 6 months.
items.notes: Whether SU itself counts as income is not stated on the borger.dk student page. 'Paid to NemKonto, CPR needed' is an inference from the NemKonto rules (NemKonto requires CPR).

items.authority: Danish public health insurance (information: Study in Denmark)
items.description: Everyone registered in the CPR (stays over 3 months) gets free GP and specialist care in Group 1 with the national health insurance card; dental care and physiotherapy are not free. EU/EEA/Swiss students must show an S1 or valid EHIC to register.

eligibility.stay_duration: over 3 months, registered in the CPR

items.amount: Free GP and hospital care (no premium)
items.how_to_apply: Automatic with CPR registration; the card arrives by post.

items.name_it: Ungdomskort, abbonamento trasporti per studenti universitari
items.description: Discounted 30-day commuter pass for travel between home and place of study for students on a full-time, SU-approved higher education programme living in Denmark (or the Oresund region / Flensburg zone), with travel time up to 3.5 hours each way.

other: full-time programme approved for SU
not during leave or paid internships
non-EU students on a study permit: receiving Ungdomskort may affect the right to stay (check nyidanmark.dk)
no travel reimbursement under other rules at the same time

items.amount: DKK 718 per 30 days (2026) when the normal commuter-card price is at most DKK 2,692; above that, DKK 718 + half the amount over DKK 2,692 (outlying municipalities always DKK 718)
items.how_to_apply: Step 1: approval at ungdomskort.uddannelsesstoette.dk; step 2: order and pay at mitungdomskort.dk, at least 14 days before use.
items.deadline: Apply at least 14 days before you need the card
items.stackable: Not combinable with other public travel reimbursement.
items.notes: The conditions page does not state whether exchange students qualify; the programme must be SU-approved.

items.description: Tax-free personal allowance shown on your main tax card (per month or per two weeks), so income tax is only withheld above it. The 8% labour-market contribution (AM-bidrag) is still due on wages, but not on SU.

other: applies to the main tax card; a secondary card has no allowance
conditions for people only partly taxable in Denmark not checked

items.how_to_apply: Automatic via the tax card / preliminary income assessment in E-tax (TastSelv).
items.stackable: Applies to all income on the main tax card (job or SU, whichever is largest).

items.name_it: SU per periodi di studio all'estero (es. Erasmus in uscita)
items.description: Students entitled to SU can take it with them on a study stay or exchange abroad that is part of their Danish education (typically a semester); SU can also be applied for a full degree abroad, and at master's level sometimes a grant toward tuition (udlandsstipendium). Relevant only for students already entitled to Danish SU; no host-country top-up for incoming Erasmus students was found.

other: must be entitled to Danish SU
the stay/programme must be approved for SU

items.how_to_apply: Apply via su.dk / minSU; programmes not on the Fast Track list can take several months to approve.
items.notes: Incoming Erasmus+ students are funded by their home country; the KU, DTU and AU pages opened list no extra grant for incoming exchange students.

items.name_local: Danish Government Scholarship – University of Copenhagen
items.name_it: Borsa del governo danese – Università di Copenaghen
items.description: Full tuition waiver plus a monthly living allowance for highly qualified non-EU/EEA master's students on a time-limited Danish study permit. Financial need is not considered; University Management decides which programmes offer it each year.

other: citizen of a country outside the EU, EEA and Switzerland (Swiss excluded)
admitted to a UCPH master's programme
not entitled to SU or to equal rights with Danish citizens

items.amount: Full tuition waiver + DKK 11,225/month living allowance for 22 months (2026 level)
items.how_to_apply: Automatic: all admitted non-EU/EEA applicants are considered; nominees are notified in the application portal.
items.deadline: Offer must be accepted within the deadline stated in the offer

items.name_local: Tuition fee waiver for non-EU/EEA MSc students – DTU
items.name_it: Esenzione dalle tasse per studenti magistrali extra-UE – DTU
items.description: A limited number of tuition fee waivers each year for new non-EU/EEA MSc students with excellent academic results, autumn intake only.

other: new MSc student, autumn intake
excellent Bachelor's-level academic record

items.amount: Tuition fee covered for two years (page does not mention a living grant)
items.how_to_apply: Upload a separate personal statement with the MSc application clearly stating you apply for the waiver, focused on Bachelor's academic achievements.

items.name_it: Borse statali danesi – Università di Aarhus
items.description: State-funded scholarships for non-EU/EEA fee-paying master's students with excellent academic qualifications, usually only one or two per programme. Arts and Aarhus BSS: tuition waiver + monthly living grant; Natural Sciences and Technical Sciences: tuition waiver only. EU/EEA/Swiss students cannot apply.

other: liable to pay tuition fees
master's programme; tied to that programme

items.amount: Full or partial tuition waiver; living grant at Arts and Aarhus BSS (amount not stated on the page)
items.how_to_apply: Automatic with the master's application; no separate documents.
items.deadline: Admission application by 15 January (summer intake) or 15 September (winter intake); if no waiver offered by 1 April / 1 November, tuition must be paid
items.notes: With a waiver only, you must still document sufficient funds for the residence permit.
